- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#9 ("Figure inputs: C8 population, absolute R2 of log RMSE, or_fit question") by `experiment-repo`  > Item 3 (the fitted-parameter oracle): `results/or_fit_check.csv` is on paper-repo `dev` (962bb32). It reruns the "OR (fit)" oracle on mechanisms (c) (kappa, true 3) and (e) (rho, true 0.5) at d = 5, 20, 80, p = 0.5, s = 0.5, sigma = 0.5, 1200 draws (4 graph draws x 300 assignments), and records RMSE of DM, of the oracle with the true parameter and of the oracle with the fitted parameter.
  > 
  > What it shows: the fit is a conditioning problem of the least-squares objective, not a coding fault. RMSE of the fitted oracle against the known-parameter oracle: (c) 0.087 vs 0.087 at d = 5, 0.549 vs 0.233 at d = 20, 2.00 vs 0.541 at d = 80; (e) 0.338 vs 0.138, 0.640 vs 0.322, 1.052 vs 0.644. The share of draws where the selected parameter sits at an end of the grid is 5% for (c) at d = 5 and 59% / 86% at d = 20 / 80 (for (e): 59%, 82%, 86%). The median spread of the SSE over the grid relative to its minimum is 0.003 at d = 5 and 0.0005 / 0.0001 at d = 20 / 80 for (c) (0.004, 0.0009, 0.0004 for (e)): the objective is nearly flat, so the parameter is not identified at higher degree. The CSV also holds RMSE of the oracle with the parameter held fixed at each grid value, so a figure can show the oracle as a curve over the grid and not as one point.
  > 
  > Draw it as: known-parameter oracle (reference), fitted-parameter oracle (worse at d >= 20, and say why in the caption: flat objective, selection at the grid end). Together with the earlier comment here (C8 population, absolute R2, `diagnostic_absolute.csv`) every item of this request is delivered; closing.
